mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT keep drifting upward from their current depressed levels, weekday foot traffic will expand and retail visits will rise over the next four weeks. The mechanism fails if workplace mobility stalls or reverses before commuting normalizes.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next 28 days while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise from their t-0w levels.

mechanism_narrative: A continued rise in RESIDENTIAL time signals stronger stay-at-home substitution, reducing discretionary retail trips over the next one to two weeks. The signal breaks if residential time falls back toward baseline while retail remains depressed.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 14 days despite RESIDENTIAL remaining above its current t-0w value.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS mobility jumps sharply above its recent range, leisure substitution pulls trips away from retail and recreation over the next two weeks. The mechanism fails if park use rises without any subsequent drop in retail visits.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall relative to the last 14 days after a week-on-week PARKS increase exceeding 5 points.

mechanism_narrative: If both GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC worsen together, consumers are responding to broad mobility restraint that also suppresses nonessential shopping. The effect should appear within one week and be strongest when grocery trips are also falling.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 7 days even though GROCERY_PHARM remains below its recent weekly mean.

mechanism_narrative: A seasonal rebound in PARKS after prolonged winter suppression precedes a lagged rebound in retail-and-recreation as outdoor activity restores short discretionary trips. The effect acts over four weeks and should fail outside the winter-to-spring transition.
candidate_trigger: PARKS turns upward for two consecutive weeks after a period below -45
evidence_refs: fact:parks remain near -40 to -52 across the four observed weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays flat or declines over the next 28 days after PARKS posts two consecutive weekly increases from a sub-45 baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES indicates commuting recovery, which expands opportunistic shopping after work and raises retail mobility within four weeks. The claim fails if only one of the two series improves or if transit recovers without workplace participation.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not outperform its prior 28-day average over the next 28 days despite simultaneous increases in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM falls while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, households are consolidating essential trips and avoiding discretionary errands, which pulls RETAIL_REC lower within two weeks. The signal fails when residential time does not remain above its recent average.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM drops below -35 while RESIDENTIAL stays above 17
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 14 days even though GROCERY_PHARM remains below -35 and RESIDENTIAL remains above 17.

mechanism_narrative: A renewed decline in TRANSIT after an already weak baseline signals tighter movement constraints, and retail-and-recreation will fall further over the next four weeks. The hypothesis fails if transit stabilizes while retail continues to deteriorate for unrelated reasons.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls at least 3 points below its prior weekly mean
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline relative to the last 28 days after TRANSIT posts a drop of at least 3 points from its prior weekly mean.
